title: Who Is PSCC - and Why a Notice Might Have Been Received | User | malvern-online.com
text:
Those who have recently received a notice from PSCC and wondered, “Who is this?” or questioned the legitimacy—such as searching terms like “PSCC Scam Letter”—are not alone. In today’s climate, skepticism is understandable, and the organization welcomes the opportunity to provide clarity.
PSCC, or Public Safety Crime Center, is a national outreach and consulting organization dedicated to promoting access to trusted anti-crime services. The group works closely with law enforcement, security experts, and communities to connect people with tools that help reduce theft, property loss, and other criminal activity.
Outreach efforts are based on real crime data, with a focus on areas experiencing higher-than-average rates of vehicle theft and property-related crimes. If a notice was sent, it’s likely because data showed the neighborhood could benefit from added awareness and prevention strategies.
PSCC was founded by professionals with deep roots in public safety. It is partially owned and founded by a respected veteran in the security field who has spent decades working alongside law enforcement and intelligence agencies. It is also partially owned and led by a woman committed to bridging the gap between communities and crime prevention resources. Transparency and integrity are key values, and the organization takes great care in the partnerships it forms and the services it promotes.
One of its owners, Pedro Palomino, is a combat veteran and security specialist who has seen firsthand how today’s criminals operate. “These criminals in these times are some of the worst and most sophisticated civilians have ever seen,” he says. “It will take all of us working together to create meaningful change.”
PSCC encourages individuals, dealerships, and insurers to take a more proactive role in security. While manufacturer features and insurance offer some protection, modern threats often require more layered solutions. Even when theft is covered, victims can still face serious financial losses, delays, and stress.
That’s why PSCC promotes a multi-layered approach—combining deterrents, tracking tools, visible markings, and access to national recovery networks. These tools are meant to enhance, not replace, existing coverage.
As a connector between trusted anti-crime resources and the public, PSCC supports a smarter, community-driven response to rising crime. Those taking time to learn more are already playing a part in building safer neighborhoods.
